---
title: "Getting set up"
---

Create a virtual environment from a checkout of the integration branch:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python examples/coverage_adjustment.py
```

This example uses synthetic counts to demonstrate measurement, inverse weights
and validation. Install `.[dev]` for tests, `.[grouped]` for frequentist random
intercepts, `.[bayesian]` for Bambi/PyMC, `.[latent]` for CmdStanPy, and `.[plot]`
for geographic plots. Latent sampling also requires CmdStan; see the README.

The Census example uses the separate `debiaspydata` companion. The README pins
the tested revision. Start with `debiaspy_example_data(n_areas=25)` for a small
subset, or use `n_areas=None` for all available areas. Covariates and centroids
are required companion assets. The loader selects areas by combined observed
and benchmark flow volume and constructs coverage from their OD margins.

For your own data, supply observed flows, benchmark flows and coverage as
DataFrames or run the portable CSV example in the README. Read the
[input guide](../inputs.md) for units, identifiers and matching requirements.
